questions.q: What does uploading a ZIP file through File Import and Export actually accomplish?
options: It creates live application records immediately
It automatically runs the product-specific import process
It places the file into UCM, under the chosen account — nothing about Oracle Fusion's application data changes yet
It deletes any previously uploaded files
questions.explain: The upload step only moves the file into the content repository. No interface table or application table is touched until later scheduled processes run.

questions.q: What scheduled process is submitted to move data from an uploaded UCM file into an interface table?
options: Import Payables Invoices
Load Interface File for Import
AutoInvoice Import
Mass Additions Create
questions.explain: Load Interface File for Import is the single, reused process that loads data from UCM into the interface table(s) matching the import process you specify.

questions.q: Why does Load Interface File for Import need an 'import process' parameter?
options: It doesn't — the parameter is purely cosmetic
Because it sets the file's upload date
Because it determines the color of the confirmation email
Because this parameter tells the process which interface table structure the uploaded CSV rows belong in
questions.explain: The import process parameter is how the system knows which interface table(s) should receive the rows from the uploaded file.

questions.q: A user runs Load Interface File for Import and it reports success. What can they conclude?
options: The data cleared the file-format hurdle and is now staged in an interface table, but no live application record has been created yet
Their journal has posted to the general ledger
Their suppliers now exist as live, active records
Nothing happened at all
questions.explain: Success at this stage only confirms the data is now staged in an interface table. A separate, product-specific import process is still required to create real records.

questions.q: What is the most important thing to remember about 'success' reported by Load Interface File for Import?
options: It is identical to the data being fully imported into the application
It means the file was permanently deleted from UCM
It only means the data is staged in an interface table, which is why confusing it with final success is a common mistake
It guarantees zero rows will ever be rejected later
questions.explain: This lesson stresses that staging success and final import success are two separate claims — mistaking one for the other is a common source of confusion.
